goal: unnamed characters of «Побег из Иннсмута» get invented names so the Keeper does not have to invent them at the table (Р-150), group profiles and stock types get a list of ready names (Р-151). «Маски Ньярлатхотепа» are not touched now.
extra:
## This work

- **One person without a name** (`pobeg-iz-innsmuta-ru/character/chakhlyy-gibrid`): give an invented name: `name.ru` (and `name.en` in Latin letters), the book's designation («Чахлый гибрид») goes to `aliases`, flag `editorial_text`, `quality.notes` gets «имя придумано (Р-150), в книге — «Чахлый гибрид»». The id never changes.
- **Group profiles and stock types** (the other files of your unit): do not rename them; add `names` — 4–6 invented names (Russian spelling, as the book spells English names) right after `stock_type`, flag `editorial_text`, and a `quality.notes` sentence «готовые имена придуманы (Р-151)». For a profile of several kinds (officer and sailor), the names fit all of them.
- **Names fit the people**: 1928, Massachusetts. Innsmouth townsfolk and hybrids — old New England Yankee names, typical of a decaying port (Obed, Zadok, Ezra, Asa, Hiram…, surnames like Pickett, Coffin, Hale, Trask, Lovering…), never the families the book already names (Marsh, Waite, Gilman, Eliot, Orne, Billingham, Sargent, Martin…; grep `kb/books/pobeg-iz-innsmuta-ru/characters/` for every surname you use). Falcon Point fishermen — old New England fishermen. US Navy, Coast Guard and Marine Corps of 1928 — ordinary American names of the time, mixed origins (Irish, Italian, Polish, Scandinavian…), no names of existing records. Use each invented name only once across all files.
- Each change of an existing record goes to its `corrections` (field, from, to, reason «Р-150» / «Р-151», ref «Р-150» / «Р-151»).
- Read the book pages where each profile appears (grep its name) only to know who they are; the names themselves are not from the book.
